claims.text: A Job creates a Pod from its template and is complete once the Pod terminates successfully (all containers exit 0); with the default single completion it creates no further Pods after that.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Workloads > Controllers > Jobs (Running an example Job; Job termination and cleanup)

claims.text: spec.backoffLimit is the number of retries before a Job is marked failed; after the limit is reached the Job gets condition Failed and creates no more Pods. With restartPolicy: Never each retry is a new Pod; the container is not restarted in place.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Jobs > Handling Pod and container failures; Pod backoff failure policy

claims.text: A Deployment's Pod template allows only restartPolicy Always, so a container that exits is restarted inside the same Pod; a Deployment's Pods exist to keep running, unlike a Job's.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Deployments > Writing a Deployment Spec > Pod Template (only restartPolicy Always is allowed)

claims.text: A CronJob creates a Job from spec.jobTemplate each time spec.schedule comes round; its 5 fields are minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week, * = every value; '0 2 * * *' = minute 0, hour 2, daily; without timeZone, the kube-controller-manager's local time zone.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Workloads > CronJob > Schedule syntax; Time zones

claims.text: concurrencyPolicy: Forbid — the CronJob does not start a new Job of its own while the Job of its previous run is still running (it governs only that CronJob's Jobs, not Jobs created by hand).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: CronJob > Writing a CronJob spec > Concurrency policy

claims.text: A CronJob does not re-run a failed Job: retries belong to the Job (backoffLimit); the CronJob's next Job comes at the next scheduled time.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: CronJob > CronJob limitations; Jobs > Pod backoff failure policy
